gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much added screen area each option gives per pound carried: on the makers' and Macworld's figures, Plugable's 15.6-inch freestanding display gives about 56 sq in per lb with its cover, the Trio 3 Pro about 43, and the Duex Float 2 Pro about 40. None states how many watt-hours a screen powered over the laptop's USB-C cable takes from the laptop's battery in a 3-hour class block (about 13.5 Wh at Mobile Pixels' 4.5 W rating for the Duex Max).
standout_why: I opened itechguides' '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' (cited) and Macworld's 'Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026' (cited). TechRepublic, the other cited page, returned HTTP 403 and was not read. itechguides gives a few weights (KYY 15.6-inch 1.7 lb, Duex Float 2 Pro 2.9 lb) but no power draw and no derived figure. Macworld gives weights for the Duex Float 2 Pro (2.9 lb), the Trio 3 Pro (4.13 lb) and Plugable's 15.6-inch display (1.35 lb bare, 1.85 lb with cover), and mentions 'laptop battery drain' without a number. Neither page computes screen area per pound or watt-hours per class. The derived figures are new, but the raw weights that drive them are already on Macworld, and I could not source weights for the light student candidates (Duex Max DS, Duex Plus DS, FOPO S1 and S7, Glance 16). So the finding only partly stands out against the rivals.
decides: Confirms that a student who carries the screen to class gets more screen per pound from a freestanding portable monitor: about 56 sq in per lb for the Plugable 15.6-inch with its cover, against about 40 to 43 for the lid-mounted Duex Float 2 Pro and Trio 3 Pro. A bus-powered single screen costs the laptop roughly 13.5 Wh over a 3-hour block. That supports ChatGPT's lean toward one light screen, and it argues against the Trio 3 Pro and the dual-screen FOPOs for daily carrying. It cannot rank the 13 to 14-inch attach-on picks (Duex Max DS, Duex Plus DS, FOPO S1 and S7) against each other, because their weights and power draw are unsourced.
